done_when: When close's merge of the default branch conflicts only in files forge sync writes, close takes the default branch's copy of those files, re-runs sync, commits the merge and continues; a conflict in any other file still stops close as today. New and existing repos: works in any repo on this release, since it uses the repo's own sync output. One command-level test: two branches that both changed the skill template merge through close without stopping, and a conflict in a code file still stops it.

findings.body: This earlier finding remains open. When close runs from a Forge source worktree using its checkout's code, a conflict in `src/forge/*.py` leaves markers in the modules that `sync.files()` parses. Passing the clean default worktree does not redirect that scan: `src/forge/sync.py:317–322` reads modules under `forge.__path__`. The resulting `SyntaxError` bypasses `merge --abort` and the normal conflict instructions, leaving the checkout in an active merge that subsequent Forge commands cannot parse. Classify these conflicts without parsing conflicted modules, or ensure inventory failures abort the merge and preserve the existing refusal behavior.
findings.title: Abort source-code conflicts before scanning live Forge modules

findings.body: This earlier finding remains open. `src/forge/githooks.py:74` includes `CLAUDE.md` in sync's inventory only when it exists. After the default branch's sync deletes it, the inventory here omits it, so a worker modification produces a modify/delete conflict that close incorrectly treats as outside sync's output. The same omission affects staging at line 278: if the worker alone added `CLAUDE.md`, recovery for another generated conflict runs sync and deletes it, but excludes that deletion from staging, leaving obsolete content committed and a dirty checkout. Include sync-managed deletion paths even when absent from the default tree.
findings.title: Include sync-managed deletions absent from the default tree

why: When forge close merges the default branch, the copies of the skill and guide that forge sync writes conflict on almost every busy day, and close stops until someone takes main's copy and re-runs sync by hand
